2. The brief facts of the case of the plaintiffs as averred in the suit plaint are as follows:-
The plaintiff No.1 is the absolute owner of suit 'A' schedule property.
She has acquired the same through gift deed dated 16.01.2014 executed by her husband G.Jagadish.
On the basis of the gift deed, 'B' Khatha of the suit 'A' schedule property is changed in the name of plaintiff No.1 and she has been paying taxes with respect to suit 'A' schedule property.
The plaintiff No.2 is absolute owner of suit 'B' schedule property and she has acquired the said property through registered gift deed executed by her father G.Jagadish on 16.01.2014.
'B' Khathaof the suit 'B' schedule property is standing in the name of plaintiff No.2 and she has been paying the taxes with respect to the suit 'B' schedule property.
G.Jagadish had acquired both the suit schedule properties through the registered sale deed dated 08.08.2013 executed by its previous owner Sri.Thimmaiah, Smt.Lakshmikanth, Sanjay Kumar and L.Archana.
Rectification deed dated 13.01.2014 was also executed in favour of G.Jagadish.
'B' Khatha of the suit schedule properties was st anding in the name of G.Jagadish and he was paying the taxes to the BBMP with respect to the suit schedule properties.

The original owner of the suit schedule properties namely Byrappa had Smt.Jagadamba vs The Commissioner on 17 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/197138540/
2 acquired the suit schedule property through the registered partition deed dated 10.06.1968.
He has executed gift deed in favour of his daughter Mudduramakka on 14.03.1978 with respect to suit schedule properties.
After the death of Mudduramakka, her son Thimmaiah, daughter R.Lakshmikantha and her legal heirs have jointly executed Sale Deed in favour of G.Jagadish.

After the death of Mudduramakka, her legal heirs namely Thimmaiah, Lakshmikantha, Sanjay Kumar and L.Archana have jointly executed irrevocable general power of attorney and affidavit dated 26.03.2007 in favour of G.Jagadish with respect to the schedule properties and put the G.Jagadish in possession and enjoyment of the suit schedule properties.
G.Jagadish has dug borewell and constructed A.C.Sheet roofed house in each schedule properties and obtained the electricity connection from the concerned authority.

Some of the officials of BBMP have came to the suit schedule properties and they have issued notice dated 13.08.2014 to the husband of plaintiff No.1 directing him to quit and vacate the schedule properties alleging that the schedule properties belongs to BBMP.
Even though the plaintiffs have produced all the documents pertaining to the suit schedule properties standing in their name, the defendants have neglected to verify those documents.
On 22.08.2014, some of the officials of BBMP have came to suit schedule property and they are threatening the plaintiffs with dire consequences.
Hence, it is stated that cause of action arose to file the suit.
As such, the plaintiffs have prayed to decree the suit.
3. After service of the suit summons, the defendants No.1 and 2 have appeared through one counsel.
The defendants No.3 and 4 have appeared through one counsel.
The defendant No.5 did not appeared before the court inspite of service of suit summons and he was placed exparte.
The defendants No.1 and 2 have filed their common written statement.
The defendant No.3 has filed separate written statement and additional written statement.
4. The defendants No.1 and 2 in their written statement have denied the contention of the plaintiffs that they are the absolute owners in possession of the suit schedule properties.
The defendants have also specifically denied the allegations of their interference with the peaceful possession and enjoyment of the suit property by the plaintiffs as alleged in the suit plaint.
The defendants No.1 and 2 in their written statement have contended that the suit 'A' and 'B' schedule properties are not private properties.

Government of Karnataka has acquired Sy.No.79/5, measuring 1 acres 1 gunta for the purpose of a residential layout to be formed by bank officers and Officials House Building Co-operative Society and has handed over the same to the beneficiaries.

The approving authority i.e.
BDA has reserved this particular Sy.No.79/5 of Doddakallasandra for the purpose of forming a playground and a park.
The BDA has handed over the said area to the defendants.

The defendants No.1 and 2 have admitted the contention of the plaintiffs that the defendant No.2 had inspected area reserved for play ground and park and noticed that G.Jagadish, the husband and father of plaintiffs No.1 and 2 respectively was in unauthorized possession of the suit schedule properties.

As such,
notice was issued to him on 13.08.2014 calling upon him to vacate the suit schedule property as the same as earmarked for development into a playground and park. The defendants No.1 and 2 in their written statement have further contended that G.Jagadish has given reply to the said notice on 20.08.2014 by contending that the land in question belongs to him and that he has not trespassed Smt.Jagadamba vs The Commissioner on 17 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/197138540/
3 the land meant for development.
The defendants No.1 and 2

in their written statement have further contended that the officials of House Building Co-operative Society have filed suit bearing O.S.No.5954/2012 against the Keshav Murthy and others for declaration to declare the Sale Deed relied upon by the defendants in the said suit is null and void and consequently restraining the defendants for interfering with the physical possession of the CA site in question.
The said suit came to be decreed on 01.06.2012.
No appeal is filed against the dismissal order.
The suit schedule properties are belonging to the ownership of BDA and now handed over to the defendant for developmental works.

The defendants No.1 and 2 in their written statement have further contended that the allegation made in the suit plaint that the officials of defendants have came to the suit property and threatened the plaintiffs that they will dispossess them from the suit schedule properties as false.
The suit is not maintainable for non-compliance of mandatory provision of Sec.482 of KMC Act.
On these among other grounds, the defendants No.1 and 2 have prayed to dismiss the suit with cost.

5. The defendant No.3 in his written statement has contended that it is a Co-operative society registered under the provisions of Karnataka Co-operative Societies Act, 1960, formed for the purpose of acquiring the land through government to form the layout and to distribute the sites to its members.

The defendant No.3 in his written statement has further contended that Sy.No.79/5A of Doddakallasandra village notified for acquisition under provisions of Land Acquisition Act by the government of Karnataka in favour of the defendant No.3 society for the purpose of forming a residential layout with all amenities.
After completion of acquisition proceedings the land so acquired were handed over to the society.
The defendant No.3 society formed the layout and allotted housing sites to its members.
The society has also provided civic amenities for the better enjoyment of its members.

The suit schedule property is a civic amenity land left by the society as the playground for the beneficial enjoyment of the layout residents and several members who have purchased sites in the layout.
It has developed the lands by forming sites as per the plan approved by the BDA.
The plaintiffs have no right, title or interest and possession over the suit property.
The plaintiffs have filed false suit against the society.
The unscrupulous officers in the office of BBMP have helped the plaintiffs to obtain 'B' Khatha reflecting a non-existent property.
The plaintiffs on the basis of concocted and created documents are trying to create semblance of right over the pubic property.

The defendant No.3 in his written statement has further contended that some of the officers of the corporation are hand in glove with the plaintiff and hence, the defendants No.1 and 2 are also not seriously contesting the matter.
The defendant No.3 in his written statement has further contended that the suit for mere injunction without seeking for relief of declaration is not maintainable.

The society and some of the residents of layout after coming to know the same, file a suit for declaration in O.S.No.5754/2005 seeking for cancellation of the Sale Deed and the court has granted the relief protecting the beneficial interest of the society and its members.

The defendant No.3 in his written statement has further contended that since portion of the land in Sy.No.79/5A is earmarked for civic amenity purpose i.e. for playground, the children of the members of defendant No.3 are using the land as playground.
The plaintiffs are now trying to prevent the residents from using the land as playground on the basis of concocted and created and sham documents.
The defendant No.3 has denied all other averments and allegations made in the suit plaint.
The defendant No.3 in his written statement has further contended that no cause of action arose to file the suit and cause of action shown in the suit plaint is false.
